Spherical angular sampling turns squared rotation-block energies into Dirichlet(1,...,1) with extra odd-coordinate Dirichlet shape 1/2. Direct Dirichlet integration proves Mellin moments finite iff s>-2, and gamma multiplication gives independent Beta(1,b) product law for R². The Mellin transform at z=1 has pole order N-1 (even D) or N (odd D), producing sharp r² log^(N-2) versus r² log^(N-1) lower tails. Near the unique balanced maximum, the constrained quadratic form has Gram determinant N; the odd extra Beta(1/2,N) endpoint density adds an epsilon^(1/2) factor. Independent gamma/beta-product moment equalities and two analytically independent formulas for both sharp upper constants agreed for N=3,4,5. Monte Carlo in supplied verify_torus_volume.py is bounded corroboration only. Frequencies and nonzero radial law are scoped exactly; no mixing-time or resonant claims.
